questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. Apply for I house! It was the best decision I ever made during my stay. The cost might seem high, but food is included in the price as well as many events like camping trips and parties. Also the food is some of the best quality you will find on Berkeley campus.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A two-stage process where full-time Berkeley students are prioritized in the first round. Be quick on the dates. some courses fill up quick. Also write professors early so they can confirm that you have the prereqs or if you are trying to enroll in graduate classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite. Be persistent, show up for lecture, and talk to your professor and you can get any class you want.

questions.answer: All imaginable kinds. Berkeley has a club for literally everything. Also they really care about american football, and there are home games every other week. There are parties every day. Taco Tueasday, Kingfish on thursdays, Monroe SF on Fridays, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Monroe SF for clubbing. It is a fun dance club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and go to bars. Talk with classmates. Living at I house gave me most of my friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Outside of the bay area public transportation is really bad. Download Uber before coming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very open-minded to meeting new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Live at I house, join all the parties you can, be prepared for course registration.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Living at I House is the single best decision you can make.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and getting to how student life can also look like (and it is much more fun than back home btw :) )
